correctness.rationale: For each fixed integer d>=3, the centered projection vector is exactly Haar-uniform on a sphere of radius 1/sqrt(2). The positive Gram matrix M of sorted gaps has explicit inverse Cartan form, determinant 1/(d+1), row sums a_j=j(d+1-j)/2. The strict entrywise monotonicity gives the exact optimizing equal-gap directions, and coarea with all (d+1)! permutation chambers and the s,q Jacobian gives the normalized exact integral. Uniform q-compactness yields the endpoint coefficient with O_d(epsilon^d) remainder and total-variation Dirichlet limit. A standalone checker verifies matrix identities and numerical tetrahedral cases; its finite checks are supplemental, not the proof.

value.rationale: The smallest projected separation is the natural one-dimensional resolution margin for representing every simplex vertex distinctly. Its exact deterministic optimum and maximizing orientation count, finite-threshold probability integral, dimension-sharp rare orientation coefficient and conditional Dirichlet allocation of slack form one motivated and nontrivial geometric-probability classification. This is a meaningful alternative to the known range-width functional, not an arbitrary parameter slice or a table recomputation.
